title: Transformation-free genome editing in plants using RNA virus vectors for CRISPR-Cas delivery
author: Lou, Xiang, et al.
materials: FastPure gel DNA extraction mini kit

steps.title: Prepare bacterial growth media
steps.instruction: Prepare LB liquid, LB agar, YEP liquid, and YEP agar media according to the listed compositions, sterilize by autoclaving, add antibiotics as needed, and store under the described conditions.

substeps.instruction: LB liquid (1 L): dissolve 10 g tryptone (1 %), 5 g yeast extract (0.5 %), and 10 g NaCl (1 %) in Milli‑Q water; adjust pH to 7.0; autoclave; add antibiotics if required; store at 4 °C for up to 1 week; handle under a laminar flow bench.

LB agar plates: add 15 g bacteriological agar to the LB liquid; autoclave at 121 °C for 20 min; cool to 55 °C; add antibiotics; mix thoroughly; pour into sterile petri dishes; let solidify; store plates inverted at 4 °C for up to 1 week.
YEP liquid (1 L): dissolve 10 g tryptone (1 %), 10 g yeast extract (1 %), and 5 g NaCl (0.5 %) in Milli‑Q water; adjust pH to 7.0; autoclave; add antibiotics as for LB; store as above.
YEP agar plates: add 15 g agar to the YEP liquid; follow the same autoclave‑cool‑add‑pour procedure as for LB agar.

steps.title: Prepare plant tissue‑culture media
steps.instruction: Prepare MS induction medium, MS induction medium with ribavirin, and MS rooting medium, adjusting pH, adding phytagel, autoclaving, cooling, and pouring plates as described.

substeps.instruction: MS induction medium (1 L): dissolve 4.4 g MS salts, 30 g sucrose, 2 mg 6‑benzylaminopurine, 2 mg 3‑Indoleacetic acid, and 0.1 mg IAA; adjust pH to 5.8; add 4 g phytagel; autoclave at 121 °C for 20 min; cool to ~50 °C; pour into plates.
MS induction + ribavirin: after autoclave and cooling to ~50 °C, add 1 mL of a 40 mg/mL ribavirin stock (final 40 µg/mL); mix gently; pour into sterile plates.

MS rooting medium (1 L): dissolve 4.4 g MS salts, 10 g sucrose, 100 mg myo‑inositol, 2 mg indole‑3‑acetic acid; adjust pH to 6.0; add 4 g phytagel; autoclave at 121 °C for 20 min; cool to ~50 °C; pour into plates.

steps.title: Prepare antibiotic and chemical stock solutions
steps.instruction: Make 50 mg/mL kanamycin, 50 mg/mL rifampicin, 40 mg/mL ribavirin, 100 mM MES (pH 5.6), 1 M MgCl₂·6H₂O, 100 mM acetosyringone, 0.2 M NaH₂PO₄·2H₂O, 0.2 M Na₂HPO₄·12H₂O, 3 M sodium acetate, 0.5 M EDTA (pH 8.0), 1 M Tris‑HCl (pH 8.0), and 0.1 % (w/v) HgCl₂, following the exact masses, volumes, pH adjustments and storage conditions.

substeps.instruction: Kanamycin: dissolve 0.5 g kanamycin in 10 mL Milli‑Q water; filter (0.22 µm); aliquot 1 mL; store at –20 °C (up to 1 yr); dilute to 50 µg/mL in media as needed.
Rifampicin: dissolve 0.5 g rifampicin in 10 mL DMSO; filter; aliquot 1 mL; store at –20 °C in the dark (up to 6 mo); dilute to 50 µg/mL in media as needed.
Ribavirin: dissolve 0.4 g ribavirin in 10 mL Milli‑Q water; filter; aliquot 1 mL; store at –20 °C in the dark (up to 1 yr); dilute to 40 µg/mL in MS induction medium.
MES buffer (100 mM, pH 5.6): dissolve 21.325 g MES monohydrate in 900 mL Milli‑Q water; adjust pH to 5.6 with KOH; bring volume to 1 L; filter; store at 4 °C in the dark (up to 6 mo).
MgCl₂ (1 M): dissolve 20.33 g MgCl₂·6H₂O in water to 100 mL; filter; store at room temperature (up to 1 yr).
Acetosyringone (100 mM): dissolve 9.81 g acetosyringone in 500 mL DMSO; aliquot 500 µL; store at –20 °C in the dark (up to 6 mo).
NaH₂PO₄ (0.2 M): dissolve 31.2 g NaH₂PO₄·2H₂O in 1 L water; store at 25 °C.
Na₂HPO₄ (0.2 M): dissolve 71.6 g Na₂HPO₄·12H₂O in 1 L water; store at 25 °C.
Sodium acetate (3 M): dissolve 40.8 g NaAc·3H₂O in 40 mL water; adjust pH to 5.2 with acetic acid; bring volume to 100 mL; autoclave; store at 25 °C.
EDTA (0.5 M, pH 8.0): dissolve 146.12 g EDTA in 800 mL water; adjust pH to 8.0 with NaOH; bring to 1 L; store at 25 °C (pH 8.0 dissolves completely).
Tris‑HCl (1 M, pH 8.0): dissolve 121.1 g Tris in 800 mL water; adjust pH to 8.0 with conc. HCl (~42 mL); bring to 1 L; autoclave; store at 25 °C.
HgCl₂ (0.1 % w/v): dissolve 0.1 g HgCl₂ in 100 mL water; store at 25 °C in the dark in a secured place; handle under a fume hood with PPE.

steps.title: Prepare working buffers for agroinfiltration and inoculation
steps.instruction: Make infiltration buffer, 0.1 M potassium phosphate buffer (pH 7.0), inoculation buffer, CTAB buffer, TE buffer, and 5× TBE buffer using the stock solutions above, following the exact component volumes and notes.

substeps.instruction: Infiltration buffer (500 mL total): mix 10 mM MES (pH 5.6) (50 mL of 100 mM stock), 10 mM MgCl₂ (50 mL of 1 M stock), 100 µM acetosyringone (500 µL of 100 mM stock), and bring to 500 mL with Milli‑Q water; prepare fresh before use.
0.1 M potassium phosphate (pH 7.0) (1 L): combine 195 mL 0.2 M NaH₂PO₄·2H₂O, 305 mL 0.2 M Na₂HPO₄·12H₂O, and water to 1 L.
Inoculation buffer (20 mL total): mix 20 mL 0.1 M potassium phosphate (pH 7.0), 0.1 g Na₂SO₃, and 20 µL 2‑mercaptoethanol (0.1 % v/v). Prepare fresh.

CTAB buffer (100 mL total): dissolve 2 g CTAB (2 % w/v), 10 mL 1 M Tris‑HCl (pH 8.0), 20 mL 0.5 M EDTA (pH 8.0), 8.2 g NaCl (1.4 M), and 2 mL 2‑mercaptoethanol (2 % v/v); add 2‑mercaptoethanol immediately before use; mix well.
TE buffer (100 mL total): combine 10 mM 1 M Tris‑HCl (pH 8.0) (1 mL), 1 mM 0.5 M EDTA (pH 8.0) (0.2 mL), and 98.8 mL water; store at 4 °C.
5× TBE buffer (1 L total): dissolve 445.8 mM Tris‑base (44.5 g), 444.7 mM boric acid (27.5 g), and 10 mM 0.5 M EDTA (pH 8.0) (20 mL); bring to 1 L with water; autoclave if desired.

steps.title: Design target sites and order oligos
steps.instruction: Retrieve target gene sequences, use CRISPOR to select 3–4 high‑efficiency protospacers (≥40 % Doench/Mor‑Mateos score, green specificity), avoid splice junctions, and order two complementary oligos with the appropriate 5′ adapters (TAGT/AAAC for Cas9, AGAT/AATT for Cas12a).

steps.title: Anneal oligonucleotides
steps.instruction: Resuspend each lyophilized oligo in 10 mM TE (pH 8.0) to 100 µM, mix 4 µL 5× annealing buffer, 2 µL forward 100 µM oligo, 2 µL reverse 100 µM oligo, and 12 µL water; heat at 95 °C for 2 min, then cool gradually to room temperature (~45 min); store dsDNA at 4 °C or freeze.

steps.title: Digest pS‑based vector with BsaI
steps.instruction: Set up a 50 µL BsaI digestion containing ~2.5 µg plasmid DNA, 5 µL 10× FastDigest buffer, 2.5 µL BsaI, and water; incubate at 37 °C for 1–2 h; purify the linearized vector by gel extraction and verify concentration.

steps.title: Ligate annealed oligos into vector
steps.instruction: In a 10 µL ligation, combine 50–100 ng linearized vector, 1 µL 1:100‑diluted annealed oligos, 1 µL 10× T4 DNA ligase buffer, 1 µL T4 DNA ligase, and water to 10 µL; incubate at 22 °C for 30 min; place on ice.

steps.title: Transform ligation into chemically‑competent E. coli DH5α
steps.instruction: Thaw 100 µL competent DH5α on ice, add ligation mix, incubate on ice 30 min, heat‑shock at 42 °C for 90 s, return to ice 3–5 min, add 800 µL LB, shake 37 °C 220 rpm for 1 h, centrifuge 8,000 rpm 2 min, resuspend in 100 µL LB, plate on LB agar + 50 mg/L kanamycin, incubate 37 °C 14 h; store plates at 4 °C up to 3 days.

steps.title: Screen colonies by colony PCR
steps.instruction: Pick a single colony with a sterile tip, streak onto a new kanamycin plate, then swirl the remaining cells into a PCR tube containing 20 µL master mix (1 µL 10 µM Nos/F primer, 1 µL 10 µM Oligo/R1 or R2, 10 µL 2× Rapid Taq Master Mix, water to 20 µL); run PCR (95 °C 3 min; 25–30 cycles of 95 °C 15 s, 50–60 °C 15 s, 72 °C 15 s/kb; 72 °C 5 min; hold 4 °C); analyze 1 % agarose gel (expected 268 bp for pS‑sg:GFP, 291 bp for pS‑cr:GFP).

steps.title: Grow positive clones and isolate plasmid DNA
steps.instruction: Inoculate a confirmed positive colony into 5 mL LB + 50 µg/mL kanamycin; shake 37 °C 220 rpm for 14 h; perform a miniprep (≈3 µg plasmid per prep); verify insert by Sanger sequencing.

steps.title: Transform Agrobacterium with viral and VSR constructs
steps.instruction: Electroporate or chemically transform Agrobacterium tumefaciens with the three binary TSWV plasmids (pL, pM‑Cas9/Cas12/ABE/CBE, pS‑sg:GFP or pS‑cr:GFP) and the three VSR plasmids (pGD‑p19, pGD‑P1/Hc‑Pro, pGD‑γb); select on appropriate antibiotics; grow overnight cultures for agroinfiltration.

steps.title: Agroinfiltrate N. benthamiana leaves
steps.instruction: Resuspend each Agrobacterium culture in infiltration buffer to an OD₆₀₀ of ~0.5–0.8, mix the three viral constructs with the three VSR cultures in equal volumes, incubate 2–3 h at room temperature, then infiltrate the abaxial side of fully expanded N. benthamiana leaves using a needleless syringe; maintain plants under growth conditions until systemic symptoms appear.

steps.title: Harvest sap and mechanically inoculate target hosts
steps.instruction: When systemic infection is evident in N. benthamiana, collect infected leaf tissue, grind in inoculation buffer, filter to obtain sap, and rub‑inoculate leaves of tobacco, tomato, pepper, ground cherry, or peanut; monitor for systemic symptoms in the new hosts.

steps.title: Regenerate edited plants from infected tissue
steps.instruction: Excise ~0.5‑1 cm leaf explants from symptomatic host plants, place epidermal side down on MS induction medium (with ribavirin if desired); incubate under standard tissue‑culture conditions until shoots emerge; transfer shoots to MS rooting medium; grow until robust roots develop.

substeps.instruction: Dissect leaf explants and position on solid MS induction medium.
Incubate until shoot induction (typically 2–4 weeks); note any albino shoots indicating PDS knockout.
Transfer each shoot to MS rooting medium; grow until well‑developed roots appear.

steps.title: Extract total DNA from infected leaves
steps.instruction: Collect ~0.1 g symptomatic leaf tissue into a 2 mL tube with two steel beads; freeze in liquid nitrogen and grind to powder; add 600 µL CTAB buffer (with freshly added 2‑mercaptoethanol), vortex, incubate 65 °C 1 h (mix every 15 min); add 600 µL chloroform:isoamyl alcohol (24:1), vortex, incubate 25 °C 10 min, centrifuge 10 000 rpm 5 min at 4 °C; transfer ~500 µL supernatant, add equal volume pre‑chilled isopropanol and 1/10 volume 3 M NaAc (pH 5.2); mix, incubate –30 °C 1 h; centrifuge 13 000 rpm 10 min 4 °C, discard supernatant; wash pellet twice with 1 mL 75 % ethanol (centrifuge 12 000 rpm 5 min 4 °C each); air‑dry, dissolve in 50 µL TE buffer; measure concentration spectrophotometrically; store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Amplify target loci for Sanger sequencing
steps.instruction: Design primers (300–500 bp amplicon; use homolog‑specific primers for polyploids); set up 50 µL PCR with 100 ng DNA, 1.5 µL each primer (10 µM), 25 µL 2× TOROBlue Flash KOD Dye Mix, water to volume; run: 98 °C 30 s; 25–30 cycles of 98 °C 10 s, X °C 25 s (primer Tm), 68 °C 10 s/kb; final 68 °C 5 min; hold 4 °C; verify on 1 % agarose gel, gel‑purify (elute in water, not TE); ensure >100 ng/µL; submit for Sanger sequencing.

steps.title: Analyze Sanger data with ICE
steps.instruction: Upload control (uninoculated) and experimental (infected) trace files to the ICE web tool (https://ice.synthego.com); enter the guide sequence (including PAM) as the GUIDE SEQUENCE; run analysis to obtain editing efficiency; alternatively use TIDE.

steps.title: Deep‑sequencing workflow for editing frequency
steps.instruction: Design primers with 5′ adapters (forward: 5′‑GGAGTGAGTACGGTGTGC‑3′; reverse: 5′‑GAGTTGGATGCTGGATGG‑3′); amplify target (150–300 bp, max 500 bp) using the PCR conditions of step 33; perform a second PCR with Illumina index primers to barcode each library; quantify libraries with a fluorometer, dilute to 1 ng/µL; pool and sequence on Illumina HiSeq; demultiplex, trim adapters, filter low‑quality reads; align to reference using Hi‑Tom; apply a 1 % mutation filter for indels and 0.1 % for base edits.
